messages:
Maria: Heads-up — our 3-year reserved instances for p4d in us-west-2 have staggered expiries starting in ~28 days. Renewal quote looks ~18% higher vs current.
Jon: Oof. Do we have the exact expiration batch breakdown?
Maria: I uploaded a quick CSV to the finance folder: https://redwood.internal/sheets/ri-expiry-2026. Columns: ri_id, region, instance_type, end_date, utilization_pct.
Kevin: Running a quick query to validate utilization. `aws ec2 describe-reserved-instances --filters Name=state,Values=active --query 'ReservedInstances[?End>=`2026-04-01`]'` — will paste results.
infra-bot: [alert] 6 RI contracts >75% utilized expiring between 2026-04-25 and 2026-05-10. Potential capacity gap if not replaced.
Amelia: Can we stagger replacements across weeks to avoid procurement spike + capacity churn? Also want to avoid buying identical region-only RIs if we plan to shift capacity to eu-west-1 later this year.
Sam: From finance POV, conversions to Compute Savings Plans would give us region flexibility but may increase short-term spend vs deep RI discounts. Need numbers.
Jon: Proposal: 3 tracks — (A) renew top-3 high-util RIs for 1 year to keep flexibility, (B) convert two medium-util contracts to Savings Plans, (C) let one low-util expire and backfill with on-demand/burst for 3 months while shifting workload. Thoughts?
Kevin: I ran utilization per contract: top-3 are 92/88/84% — solid candidates to renew. Two mid are ~62/58% — convertible to SP might be ok. Low one is 34% — let expire.
Maria: Quick risk callout: the low-util RI is attached to a training cluster used by research. If we let it go we need an autoscaling policy change or preemptible fallback.
Jon: Actionable steps: 1) Finance to model 1yr RI vs 3yr RI vs Savings Plan for the 5 contracts (Sam). 2) Infra to prepare canary replacement playbook and capacity reservation runbook (Kevin + Amelia). 3) Ops to notify research teams about potential preemptible fallback (Maria).
Sam: I'll run the cost model this afternoon and post numbers. If SP delta <8% vs yearly RI, finance leans SP for flexibility.
Amelia: For the playbook — propose rolling replacement over 3 weeks, reserve 20% buffer capacity in other regions, and enable KV-prefetch/cache warmup before migrating. I'll draft and link here.
Kevin: Also tagging aws-costs team for potential early-purchase discounts and region pooling: @Sam @Amelia @Maria.
Maria: Adding a small script to detect utilization outliers and re-assign nodes if <40% for 2 consecutive weeks. Pasting snippet:```bash
# check RI utilization
aws ce get-reservation-utilization --time-period Start=2026-03-01,End=2026-03-31 --granularity MONTHLY --filter 'Dimensions={Key=REGION,Values=[us-west-2]}'
```
Jon: Nice. Let's sync in 2 hours for the cost numbers + draft playbook. :calendar:
Amelia: Added PR for the playbook draft: https://redwood.internal/pulls/infra/ri-playbook. Please comment. :eyes:
Maria: Thanks everyone — want minimal risk to production but also avoid multi-year lock if we expect regional shifts.
infra-bot: [ops-note] Thread tagged: capacity-planning, savings-plan-eval.
Jon: Closing loop: next check-in 15:00 PT.
thread_summary: Discussion about upcoming RI expirations for p4d in us-west-2, proposing a staggered replacement strategy combining 1yr RIs, Savings Plans, and letting a low-util contract expire. Action items assigned to finance (cost modeling), infra (playbook), and ops (notifications).
